activity.notes: Sorghaghtani was not Great Khan or sovereign ruler of 'Mongolia'. After Tolui's death, she retained and administered his family appanage, developed its sedentary revenues and became a central imperial stateswoman whose political strategy helped transfer the Great Khanate to her son Möngke. ATLAS therefore models her against the Toluid ulus rather than falsely assigning her a reign over the whole Mongol Empire.

sources.title: Sorghaghtani Beki in the eyes of court historians — World History Commons
sources.citation_text: Contemporary court historians Juvaini and Rashid al-Din are quoted describing Sorghaghtani's administration of affairs of state and the decisive political management of her sons' interests.

sources.title: The reign of Khubilai khan — The Cambridge History of China
sources.citation_text: The Cambridge History of China describes Sorghaghtani as a powerful political actor with her own north-China appanage and credits her strategy with the rise of her sons.
